(a) males with an unlimited food supply show more social display behavior than males with a limited food supply and (b) males incited by female show higher testosterone levels than males that are not incited by female.

the role of male hormone levels in male social display activity during mate selection in mallard ducks.
the relationship between social display behavior and steroid hormone levels in male mallards.
the relationship between the male's social display behavior and the levels of testosterone and dihydrotestosterone.

male mallards in good feeding condition are more attractive to females and that this attractiveness is reflected in elevated hormone levels.
